       You will read five emails.

  6      Hi Mike!
         I forgot to mention I’m flying to the Isle of Wight next month for a certified course in Graphic
         Design. I wanted to attend it last month but I was late, it was fully booked. I know it would be
         best to wait until the holidays, when it’s cheaper, but you know me, I’m so impatient! Will keep
         in touch!
         Gemma

         Why is Gemma not attending the course during the holidays?

         A Because it was sold out.
         B Because it was cheaper.
         C Because she couldn’t wait.



  7      Hiya Jen!
         What a nightmare! There was a blizzard and the train was delayed. First I was stuck in a
         carriage with a dozen other passengers and it was really stuffy, even when four of them got off
         and took the coach. When we started again, an elderly couple got on at the next stop and we
         were squeezed until we arrived at our destination. Imagine that for a holiday adventure!
         Bella

         How many passengers arrived including Bella at the final stop?

         A Four.
         B Eleven.
         C Twelve.

  8   Dear Helena,
      I loved the exhibition. You know art is my passion. What I liked was how many artists in the
      exhibition were exploring their dreams. They finally moved away from painting mythological
      scenes. The use of colour and non-traditional materials was absolutely brilliant. There was
      some confusion though about how the exhibits were displayed. Thanks for asking me.
      See you soon,
      Lisa

      What did Lisa like about the exhibition?

      A It wasn’t traditional.
      B It was well-organised.
      C It exhibited mythological themes.



  9   Hi Eric,
      So glad to hear you enjoyed the concert, too! The Choones were amazing. Despite not having
      a solid voice, the singer appeared pretty sure of himself. He put on quite a show. I used to think
      their songs weren’t catchy or romantic enough and preferred more soothing music like Colday.
      My sister changed my mind.
      Keep cool!
      Monica

      What did Monica think of the concert?

      A She prefers a different kind of music.
      B The singer’s voice was disappointing.
      C The singer’s performance was impressive.



 10   Hello Mikey!
      It’s a pity you couldn’t join the reunion. The food we were served last night was fantastic.
      The fish was absolutely mouth-watering. It made me wonder about the food I’ve been eating all
      these years. As for the price, it was reasonable, considering the exotic ingredients the master
      chef miraculously blended. We hoped it would be a bargain, since we know the restaurant
      owner, but we didn’t mind. It was a dish fit for a king!
      Lara

      What does Lara say about the cost of the dinner?

      A It was a bargain.
      B It was expensive.
      C It was medium-priced.

Task 3
       Questions 11-15

       Read the text below.
       For each question (11-15), choose the correct answer (A, B or C).
       Mark your answer on the answer sheet.


                                              Reading aloud

      While fewer children start reading in preschool with the help of their teachers, the majority begin
  reading on their own very easily as a result of their parents reading to them. However, it is not
  always that simple, and the choice of book or story by the parent is a highly important factor. For
  reading aloud to be truly beneficial to children, the chosen stories must be interesting, realistic and
  inspiring for them.
      Young children often struggle with concepts that are symbolic or abstract, such as those found
  in fantasy novels, which are much more popular with teenagers. Complex sentences and length
  can also sometimes be issues. Stories dealing with familiar, everyday experiences and characters
  they can relate to are often much easier to appreciate. Such stories also give children something
  to discuss after a book is finished and often teach them practical knowledge they can apply to their
  own lives.
      To increase vocabulary, children need to come across words that they don’t know. Puzzled
  by unfamiliar words, children will push themselves to learn because the words are important to
  the story. When parents or teachers realise they have just read an unfamiliar word, they should
  avoid explaining the definition right away. By rereading the surrounding sentences slowly, children
  can be encouraged to use context to work out the meaning of the word. This teaches them not to
  give up, which is an important skill they can use throughout their reading lives.
      When children are encouraged to read what they want, they are motivated to read more.
  Reading interesting stories aloud can help children develop the desire to read and understand
  what words have to offer – without pressuring them to learn too many words too soon. With the rise
  of the Internet and social media, reading skills are more significant than ever before. However, using
  digital tools too early can discourage reading.



 11      Who helps most children start reading independently?

         A They themselves.
         B Their teachers.
         C Their parents.

Reading Paper                                                  Engleski jezik

      A Stories that are important to them.
      B Stories that are motivating.

      C Language structures.



 14   How do children react when they first hear a new word?

      A They ignore it.
      B They feel confused.
      C They are discouraged.



 15   How are good readers developed?

      A By using digital tools.
      B By building their vocabulary.
      C By letting them choose their stories.

    Questions 16-20

    Read the text below.
    For each question (16-20), choose the answer (A-F) that best completes the sentence.
    There is one letter that you do not need. Mark your answer on the answer sheet.
    There is an example at the beginning (0→G).


                                     Japanese eco revolutionist

      The Japanese have long been a very environmentally aware nation. When Haru Hayashi was
  24 years old, he had a sudden idea that would set his life on a new track and change the world.
  This was in 1937, (0) ___. He was working as an agricultural customs inspector (16) ___. Lying
  in his hospital bed, an existential crisis took hold of him (17) ___. He could barely work, and he
  thought that nothing would change. Then, early one morning, it dawned on him.
      He quit his job and returned to the family farm, (18) ___. The essence of Hayashi’s insight was
  the emptiness of human knowledge and effort. Cultivating his father’s fruit trees, (19) ___. His
  approach was not to ask himself what more he could do to improve the produce of his trees, rather
  what practices he could do without. Nature, he believed, was a complete and unified whole,
  (20) ___. He developed a profound understanding of the ecosystem he worked in and learned how
  to flow with nature.
